title: Linking through unique student identifier
description: The student id submitted with the assignment is a unique identifier that can be used to link the submission data to a specific student across the system.
assumptions: Student id is globally unique within the educational system

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: The combination of student id, course, and submission timestamp creates a quasi-identifier set that could potentially link data to a specific individual through analysis.
assumptions: Course and timestamp combination may not be unique across all students

title: Processing of identified information via student id
description: The data flow contains a unique student identifier that directly identifies the data subject (student) submitting the assignment.
assumptions: Student id is a direct identifier of the individual

title: Quasi-identifier in submission data
description: The combination of course and submission timestamp may serve as quasi-identifiers that could identify the student when combined with other data.
assumptions: Course and timestamp combination may be unique or near-unique for some students

title: Attributable data evidence through submission timestamp
description: The submission timestamp combined with student id creates evidence that can be used to attribute the assignment submission to a specific student, preventing denial.
assumptions: Timestamp is recorded and associated with student id

title: Potentially sensitive work file data
description: The work file submitted may contain sensitive personal or academic information that exceeds what is functionally required for grade submission.
assumptions: Work file may contain more sensitive content than needed for grading

title: Potential unnecessary data treatment
description: The work file may be analyzed or enriched beyond what is necessary for the functional goal of grade submission.
assumptions: System may process file content beyond metadata extraction

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware of how their assignment data (work file, metadata) is collected, processed, and stored by the Grades Portal.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities

title: Lack of student control over data preferences
description: Students may lack control to set preferences regarding how their assignment data is processed, stored, or shared.
assumptions: No granular consent or preference mechanisms for assignment data

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The collection of work file, student id, course, and timestamp may exceed what is strictly necessary for the functional goal of grade submission.
assumptions: Work file content may be more sensitive than needed for grading purposes
